opportunities.title: 33 Zero-Days, Zero Warning: Why N-able Just Killed Its Own Cloud
opportunities.why_now: A researcher dropped 30+ unpatched N-central zero-days with working PoCs, forcing N-able to pull its hosted platform offline mid-incident.
opportunities.angle: Breach-digest deep dive on the disclosure timeline, who's exposed (MSPs managing thousands of endpoints), and what 'full-disclosure-as-pressure-tactic' means for the next vendor caught flat-footed

opportunities.title: Iran Didn't Hack a Bank — It Cooked a Supermarket's Fridges
opportunities.why_now: France officially attributed a sabotage campaign that overheated refrigeration controllers at ~700 retail sites to Iranian state actors, turning OT security into a grocery-aisle story.
opportunities.angle: Explainer on ICS/OT attack surface creeping into everyday retail, framed as 'the inevitable breach' finally hitting your shopping cart

opportunities.title: Chrome's Eighth Zero-Day This Year Just Dropped — Patch Now or Join the Stats
opportunities.why_now: Google shipped an emergency fix for an actively exploited XML zero-day, the eighth Chrome zero-day of 2026, a record-pace year for browser exploitation.
opportunities.angle: Year-in-patches tracker post/tweet thread charting all 8 Chrome zero-days with dates, CVEs, and exploitation status to show the accelerating cadence

opportunities.title: SSHole: The Auth Bypass That Turned Your SSH Server Into an Open Door
opportunities.why_now: CISA is actively warning about exploitation of the newly named 'SSHole' OpenSSH authentication bypass alongside GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, and IBM flaws all being hit in the wild simultaneously.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence alert post naming all four actively-exploited CVEs in one scannable checklist, with urgency framing for sysadmins who haven't patched this week

opportunities.title: Who Gives A Crap Indeed: Toilet Paper Company Joins the Breach Hall of Fame
